paragraphs: Natan or Rav Natan. (Natan the prophet, II Samuel ch. 12.) Abba bar Natan, Mo'ed Katan ch. 3, halakha 4.
Rav Ada (or Acha) bar Natan, Chullin 49a. Ami bar Natan—Rabbi Ami cited without further designation. Issi bar Natan, Berakhot 62a.
Rav Huna son of Rav Natan, Berakhot 42a.
Rav Chiyya son of Rav Natan, Pesachim 41a. Yehudah bar Natan, Berakhot 60a.
Rav Kahana son of Rav Natan, Yevamot 60b.
Rav Mesharshiya son of Rav Natan, Pesachim 115a. Rava bar Natan, Eruvin 32b—he is Abba bar Natan.

notes.text: This is a collective list, not a single biography. The prophet Natan is a namesake. Hyman’s Rava/Abba identification remains his claim; the cited Chiyya, Kahana and Mesharshiya passages explicitly name Rav Natan as father.
This is an index of names and patronymics, not a claim that all these men share one father or identity. Natan the prophet is a separate namesake; the Rava/Abba equation remains Hyman’s.
